title: Pods, ReplicaSets and labels
summary: The pod is the unit; labels are how everything finds everything.

steps.title: The pod
body: A **pod** wraps one or more containers that always run together on the same node and share one IP address and any volumes. Usually it is one app container, sometimes plus a **sidecar** (a log shipper, a proxy).

Pods are **cattle, not pets**: a pod is never repaired or moved. If it dies or its node dies, a *new* pod with a new name and new IP replaces it. That is why you almost never create bare pods: nothing would replace them.

steps.prompt: Two containers in the same pod need to talk to each other. Which address does the first use to reach the second, listening on port 9000?
steps.explain: Containers in a pod share one network namespace, so they see each other on `localhost`. They must not both listen on the same port.
Pods live in the core API group, written as plain `v1`. Deployments live in `apps/v1`.

steps.title: Labels and selectors
body: **Labels** are key/value tags on any object: `app=shop-api`, `tier=web`, `env=prod`. A **selector** picks objects by label. Nothing in Kubernetes refers to pods by name; ReplicaSets, Services and network policies all use selectors.
selector tier in (web), env!=dev -> A, C
A `matchLabels` selector matches a pod when **every** key/value in the selector is present on the pod. Extra labels on the pod do not matter.
A **ReplicaSet** is "keep N pods matching this selector alive, and here is the pod template for making more". You rarely write one yourself; Deployments create them.

steps.explain: Every selector pair must be present; additional pod labels are ignored.

steps.prompt: You run `kubectl label pod shop-abc12 app=debug --overwrite` on a pod owned by a ReplicaSet whose selector is `app=shop`. What happens?
options: The ReplicaSet no longer counts that pod, so it creates a replacement; the relabelled pod keeps running on its own
Nothing: ReplicaSets track pods by name
steps.explain: This is a real debugging trick: pull a misbehaving pod out of rotation (Services select by label too) while keeping it alive to inspect.

steps.prompt: A broken image name is the classic first-deploy mistake. Fill in the STATUS that `kubectl get pods` shows once the kubelet has failed to pull `shop/apii:2.0` a few times.
steps.explain: First you may see `ErrImagePull`, then `ImagePullBackOff` while it waits to retry. `kubectl describe pod` shows the real reason: *not found*, *unauthorized* (missing `imagePullSecrets`), or a typo in the registry name.

steps.title: Match a selector
prompt: Write `bool Matches(Dictionary<string, string> selector, Dictionary<string, string> labels)`: true when every key in `selector` is in `labels` with the same value. An empty selector matches everything.
Then write `List<string> Select(Dictionary<string, string> selector, Dictionary<string, Dictionary<string, string>> pods)` returning the names of matching pods, sorted.
starter: bool Matches(Dictionary<string, string> selector, Dictionary<string, string> labels)
List<string> Select(Dictionary<string, string> selector, Dictionary<string, Dictionary<string, string>> pods)
solution: bool Matches(Dictionary<string, string> selector, Dictionary<string, string> labels)
return selector.All(kv => labels.TryGetValue(kv.Key, out var v) && v == kv.Value);
List<string> Select(Dictionary<string, string> selector, Dictionary<string, Dictionary<string, string>> pods)
return pods.Where(p => Matches(selector, p.Value)).Select(p => p.Key).OrderBy(n => n).ToList();
template: var dojoPods = new Dictionary<string, Dictionary<string, string>> {
Dojo.Check("app=shop matches a pod with extra labels", Matches(new() { ["app"] = "shop" }, dojoPods["a"]), "extra labels on the pod should not matter");
Dojo.Check("app=shop,tier=db does not match pod a", !Matches(new() { ["app"] = "shop", ["tier"] = "db" }, dojoPods["a"]), "every pair must match");
Dojo.Check("missing key does not match", !Matches(new() { ["version"] = "2" }, dojoPods["a"]), "");
Dojo.Eq("Select app=shop", new List<string> { "a", "b" }, Select(new() { ["app"] = "shop" }, dojoPods));
Dojo.Eq("Select tier=web,env=prod", new List<string> { "a", "c" }, Select(new() { ["tier"] = "web", ["env"] = "prod" }, dojoPods));
Dojo.Eq("empty selector selects all", new List<string> { "a", "b", "c" }, Select(new(), dojoPods));
hints: `selector.All(kv => ...)` is true for an empty selector, which is what you want.
